title: Sign structure of an additive gate-function modification to the Friedmann equation
description: Analytical proof and numerical verification (in CLASS v3.3.4) that an additive, monotonically activating EFC gate g(z) with positive amplitude A, when closed by enforcing E(0)=1 via Ω'Λ=ΩΛ−Ag(0), yields a strictly non-positive ΔE²(z)=A[g(z)−g(0)] for all z>0. The sign-lock reduces Hubble friction and necessarily enhances structure growth, implying background-only EFC cannot suppress σ8; CLASS results agree with the analytical prediction at the <0.3% level across nine redshifts.

friedmann_standard.description: Flat-universe Friedmann equation with closure E(0)=1.

efc_background.description: Additive EFC gate modifies the background expansion with amplitude A and gate g(z).

gate_function.description: Sigmoid-like gate that activates at late times; monotonically non-decreasing in scale factor a.

closure_condition.description: Closure normalisation enforcing E_{EFC}(0)=1 by compensating the gate at z=0.

sign_lemma.latex: \Delta E^2(z) \equiv E^2_{\mathrm{EFC}} - E^2_{\Lambda\mathrm{CDM}} = A\,[g(z)-g(0)] \le 0 \quad (z>0,\ A>0,\ g\ \text{monotone in}\ a)
sign_lemma.description: Main lemma: the additive gate yields a strictly non-positive change in E^2 at all z>0.

growth_equation.description: Linear matter growth with GR source term (\mu=1 at background-only level); smaller H reduces friction and enhances growth.

key_results.main_finding: Under E(0)=1 closure with A>0 and a monotonically activating gate, ΔE²(z)≤0 for all z>0, reducing Hubble friction and increasing fσ8; CLASS verifies the analytic ΔH²=A[g(z)−g(0)]H0² with ≤0.3% discrepancy across nine redshifts.
datasets_used: CLASS v3.3.4 numerical background outputs (nine redshift points)
No observational datasets (analytical proof + code verification)

sealed_predictions.statement: For any positive A and monotonically non-decreasing gate g(a) closed by Ω'Λ=ΩΛ−Ag(0), the background-only EFC model necessarily yields Δfσ8(z)>0 relative to ΛCDM over late times (z≈0.3–1), independent of (A, z_t, n) values.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Independent Boltzmann/ODE implementation (e.g., CAMB or custom solver) showing Δfσ8≤0 for A>0, monotone g, and μ=1 under E(0)=1 closure.

sealed_predictions.statement: With E(0)=1 closure, ΔE²(z)=A[g(z)−g(0)] must be non-positive for all z>0 when A>0 and g is monotone in a.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Direct numerical evaluation of H(z) from the modified background equations producing any ΔE²(z)>0 at z>0 under the stated conditions.

kill_criteria: KC1: Numerical evaluation (double precision) of the closed model with A>0 and a monotonically non-decreasing g(a) yields ΔE²(z)>0 for any z>0, or a deviation from the analytic ΔE²=A[g(z)−g(0)] exceeding 0.5% after accounting for ncdm contributions.
KC2: A background-only implementation with μ=1, A>0, monotone g(a), and E(0)=1 produces Δfσ8(z)<0 relative to ΛCDM in a verified independent code across 0.3≤z≤1.
KC3: Closure failure: after applying Ω'Λ=ΩΛ−Ag(0), E_EFC(0)≠1 at machine precision (|E_EFC(0)−1|>1e−10) in the background solver.

KC4: Early-universe preservation failure: with the quoted parameters, the gate is not suppressed at recombination (g(z=1100)≫10^{-16}) or alters the comoving sound horizon r_s beyond 1 ppm relative to ΛCDM.

KC5: Empirical requirement for ΔH/H>0 at 0.3≲z≲1 under the restriction A>0 and monotone g(a) with E(0)=1, i.e., any data-driven background reconstruction demanding E_EFC(z)>E_ΛCDM(z) in this range, contradicting the sign-locked prediction.
abstract_short: Under standard closure normalisation E(0) = 1, the additive gate ΔE² = A[g(z) − g(0)] is strictly non-positive for all z > 0. This reduces Hubble friction and enhances structure growth. Background-level EFC cannot suppress σ₈. Verified numerically in CLASS v3.3.4 to < 0.1%.

technical_note_II.relationship: Builds on sign lemma to investigate perturbation channel

sign_verification.description: ΔH² comparison: CLASS vs analytical prediction at 9 redshift points

growth_signature.description: fσ₈ at BOSS DR12 redshifts: enhanced growth due to reduced Hubble friction

key_conclusions: ΔE²(z) = A[g(z) − g(0)] ≤ 0 for all z > 0 (Lemma 1)
H_EFC(z) ≤ H_ΛCDM(z): reduced Hubble friction enhances structure growth
Background-level EFC cannot suppress σ₈ under E(0) = 1 normalisation
Structural constraint independent of numerical values of (A, z_t, n)
